qa.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to Comanche CC2 and CC3?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists generators 2G1 at 408.8 MW and 2S1 at 277.6 MW with unit code CC2. It lists generators 3G1 at 408.8 MW and 3S1 at 277.6 MW with unit code CC3. Each pair is a gas turbine plus a steam turbine, so each pair is one combined cycle block.
qa.recommendation: Treat 2G1 and 2S1 as CC2, and 3G1 and 3S1 as CC3. Type these ids into Other IDs for the unit by hand in the web form.
qa.note: EIA's own unit code column names the blocks, so there is no doubt about the pairing. The generators are planned for September 2029 and EIA says regulatory approvals are not initiated, which is out of date because the air permit application was filed in April 2026.

qa.question: What capacity should each new Comanche block carry?
qa.finding: GEM and the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx show 686.4 MW per block. The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows 775.2 MW for each of the two queue entries ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026. The air permit application at https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ATdpa%C3%81tiBf6AUlxodMaTf4RyyKtRvO65cbkkb3aVZbN4JAjNn88hU2pksW3d3Ngw9ZE27%C3%81UOLoThr916JdkRs9c%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true says each block will produce 633 MW.
qa.recommendation: Leave 686.4 MW, which is EIA's nameplate figure. Ask the project manager whether the larger queue figure should be used because it may include duct burner output.
qa.note: The queue figure may be the interconnection request and not the nameplate. The permit figure is a total output at one set of site conditions. I did not find a document that gives the nameplate in plain terms.
